selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main claim made about a single apple in this passage?
questions.answer: Its existence and arrival as real nourishment point to a Creator whose power and rule extend far beyond that one fruit.

questions.question: Why does the passage stress that the apple is given “generously”?
questions.answer: To show that provision is not just mechanically produced but mercifully bestowed.

questions.question: What is the importance of the changing seasons in the reasoning?
questions.answer: They are part of the necessary conditions that allow fruit to grow and become available.

questions.question: What inference is drawn from the repeated signs found across living things?
questions.answer: The maker of one fruit must also be the maker of the wider world in which that fruit belongs.

questions.question: How does the passage use repetition across many created things as evidence?
questions.answer: It argues that repeated patterns of purposeful design across creation point to one Maker.

questions.question: What does this universal conclusion say about the true owner of the apple?
questions.answer: The true owner must also be the Lord of everything connected to the apple’s existence.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by calling every fruit a seal of unity?
questions.answer: Each fruit serves as a sign pointing to the oneness of its Creator.

questions.question: In what sense is the earth called the fruit’s garden and the cosmos its factory?
questions.answer: These images show different levels of environment and production involved in bringing the fruit into existence.

questions.question: What is the role of the image of a written book in the final sentence?
questions.answer: It portrays the universe as meaningful and readable, with each fruit acting like a sign from its Author.

questions.question: According to the passage, why can the giving of one apple not be explained by a limited cause?
questions.answer: Because its production depends on vast, connected systems that only a Lord over the whole world could control.

questions.question: How does the passage link nourishment with cosmic order?
questions.answer: It shows that food reaches people through the ordered functioning of the world, including time, seasons, and the earth’s movement.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by saying the earth brings seasonal fruits to waiting creatures?
questions.answer: It suggests intentional delivery of sustenance, not accidental availability.

questions.question: What is the significance of those same signs appearing on other living things too?
questions.answer: It means the same Creator is acting across all of creation, not just in one object.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the same seal appearing elsewhere?
questions.answer: It says the same kind of sign appears on all similar created things.

questions.question: What relationship does the passage establish between the apple and other creatures?
questions.answer: It presents them as belonging to the same created family under one Lord.

questions.question: In this passage, what does “unity” refer to?
questions.answer: It refers to the oneness of Allah as the sole Creator and Provider behind all things.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about the scope of the Creator’s kingship?
questions.answer: It extends over the inhabitants of the world, the earth itself, and the entire cosmos.

questions.question: How does the fruit point not only to a maker but also to the maker of the whole earth and universe?
questions.answer: Since the fruit depends on those wider realities, the one who truly makes it must also make and govern them.

questions.question: What idea about provision is highlighted through the example of the apple?
questions.answer: Even one piece of provision points to Allah’s all-encompassing power and care.

questions.question: Why does the passage move from the apple to the structure of the world?
questions.answer: Because the apple cannot be understood properly without the larger system that produces and delivers it.

questions.question: What is meant by saying the same mark found on one apple is also found on all fruits, plants, and animals?
questions.answer: The same signs of purposeful making and mercy appear throughout creation, showing one source behind all of them.

questions.question: What does the passage say can be read from the surface of an apple?
questions.answer: It can be read as a sign of wisdom, mercy, and dependence on the Creator.

questions.question: Why does the passage argue from one apple to all apples?
questions.answer: Because the same pattern found in one is found in the rest, so one example opens the way to a universal conclusion.

questions.question: What role do spring and summer play in the argument?
questions.answer: They are presented as the periods in which the fruit develops and ripens, showing that its making involves large-scale management of time and nature.
